plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped, crocus-like flowers in autumn, long after its strap-like leaves have died back in summer. The blooms emerge directly from the ground without foliage, giving it the nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe, in damp meadows and woodland edges; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust perennial wildflower with hairy stems and masses of daisy-like flowers with golden-yellow centers. It forms dense clumps and is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America in meadows, prairies, and roadsides; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies depend heavily on New England asters as a fueling stop for nectar during their autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Streets and parks become carpeted with fallen blossoms during peak bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (late September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Brisbane, Sydney, Grafton), and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and an old student superstition says a blossom falling on your head brings good luck in exams.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing clusters of tiny, intensely fragrant flowers hidden among glossy green leaves. The scent is often described as a blend of apricot, peach, and jasmine.
plants.location: Native to China and parts of Japan and the Himalayas; cultivated across East Asia, and in warm temperate gardens in the southeastern United States and Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In China, osmanthus blooms are used to flavor teas, cakes, wines, and sweet preserves, and the Mid-Autumn Festival is closely associated with its fragrance, with the city of Guilin named after the tree ('gui' means osmanthus).
